issues.title: [Refactor][MoE] Preserve A3 shared expert clamp with official DequantSwiGLU
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Experimental official CANN replacement for clipped A3 INT8 shared experts, based on main `4f3648abd258a5cbdd1a9ae34165a85f5e44beaf`, independent of #15994.

**DRAFT, NOT PRODUCTION-READY.** Two remaining blockers are explicit:

1. The adapter is still slower than the legacy fused operator. Large TP1/T64 graph replay can also regress relative to the previous adapter.
2. The existing custom `DequantSwigluQuant` package conflicts with official execution. Directly resolving the official API from `libopapi.so` or `libopapi_nn.so` did not isolate execution in our mixed-environment tests. The new binding rejects this conflict instead of returning incorrect outputs. Production coexistence needs separate operator namespacing; unsetting the entire custom OPP path would break other model operators and is not a solution.

The adapter preserves shared-expert execution; supplying one operator group does not turn shared experts into routed experts. It interleaves `[gate | up]` INT32 projections and FP32 scales, uses one group and `[1,2H]` scales, and explicitly sets dynamic quantization, `swiglu_mode=1`, `activate_left=True`, alpha/bias=1/0. Groups smaller than eight rows are repeated to eight and sliced back, retaining the measured workaround for small-shape precision failures. The underlying CANN small-shape defect is not established here.

Optimization commit `0a23664e390e76279e25843d8c1865afed451c88`:

- One native PyTorch dispatch wraps the official `aclnnDequantSwigluQuantV2`, using the repository ACLNN adapter. No new computation kernel or custom OPP is introduced.
- Executor-local prepared weight scales and token-count ranges remove repeated static preparation. Normal weight identity/pointer/version changes invalidate the weights; in-place writes to inference tensors without version counters require explicit invalidation.
- T=1 stacks expanded halves directly and expands activation scales, eliminating generic `ConstantPadNd`; other small groups repeat rows. Input values themselves are never cached.
- Runtime and symbolic Meta implementations use separate headers. Cold graph capture uses the stateless path without retaining graph-private cache allocations; old group ranges are retained for existing captured graphs when capacity grows.
- Only A3, positive limits and alpha/bias=1/0 select this adapter. Other hardware, no-limit, nondefault alpha/bias, Situ, MXFP and routed branches retain their original dispatch. The custom operator is not deleted.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible A3 calls use the official adapter only in a nonconflicting operator environment. A conflicting legacy OPP registration now raises a descriptive error rather than producing an apparently successful but incorrect replacement. The default existing custom package therefore remains a deployment blocker for this draft. No new setting or model routing change; no running service was modified or restarted.

### How was this patch tested?

**Actual NPU, single-operator scope:** host 156, Ascend910_9362, idle physical device 8 in its existing device-owning container. Each launch checked for no device process. No service stop, device reset or device-share change.

- CANN **9.2.0-beta.2, not GA**, torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4.dev20260715. Legacy and official used separate fresh processes.
- Compiled the exact production runtime and Meta headers as separate translation units, together with the current branch's ACLNN adapter dependencies, into a minimal loadable test library. This is not a full rebuild of `vllm_ascend_C` or a full-model test.
- 24 real weight-derived shared fixtures: Flash W8A8 / Pro W4A8, TP1/TP16 shard shapes, T=1/8/64, amplitudes 1/16. Fixture SHA256 `ca9cbc4c7c9ba0484785cd66535a1d6f852f955e6c7deba9fabe1413bfcde758`.
- 40 synthetic fixtures: T=1/2/3/4/5/6/7/8/9/64, widths 256/384/4096/6144. Four additional NPU quant-matmul-produced INT32 fixtures use random matrices, not actual model weights.
- Every fixture scans limits 1/2/10/100; cached and uncached paths produce **544/544 exact INT8 output and FP32 scale matches**. After negating x and halving activation_scale, all 544 also match fresh legacy; full graph capture/replay matches both original and changed input values. Cold capture/cache behavior and FakeTensor Meta checks passed. Clean official process maps show no custom OPP or CANN 9.1.
- Executed the repository test's original isolated kernel runner and assertion functions: another **192 parameterized NPU parity cases passed**. The surrounding repository-wide pytest/conftest harness was not run. The test no longer mixes legacy and official kernels in one process.
- Mixed custom-OPP environment: before adding the guard, all 544 comparisons failed, including when using the NN-specific official API library. Final cached/uncached conflict-guard tests correctly reject this environment. This is a failed coexistence experiment, not a passed official validation.
- TP16 denotes shard input shapes, not a 16-device model run. No full-model accuracy/throughput claim.

**Call-level synchronized E2E performance**, including Python/cache/native adapter and all device work: 30 warmups, seven rounds of 200 calls/replays, median microseconds, randomized old/new order inside the same process. Timing is outside the profiler. Other services on other devices remained running; host clocks/scheduling were not isolated. Raw samples and separate legacy before/after runs are retained.

| Shape, amplitude 16 / limit 10 | Previous eager us | New eager us | Change | Previous graph us | New graph us | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Flash TP1 T1 | 176.32 | 90.90 | -48.4% | 55.15 | 23.56 | -57.3% |
| Flash TP1 T8 | 154.35 | 72.76 | -52.9% | 20.26 | 17.77 | -12.3% |
| Flash TP1 T64 | 152.86 | 69.05 | -54.8% | 29.30 | 34.27 | +17.0% |
| Flash TP16 T1 | 176.18 | 90.41 | -48.7% | 49.96 | 19.61 | -60.8% |
| Flash TP16 T8 | 150.75 | 70.37 | -53.3% | 16.33 | 13.61 | -16.6% |
| Flash TP16 T64 | 149.55 | 71.16 | -52.4% | 20.71 | 18.28 | -11.7% |
| Pro TP1 T1 | 179.99 | 92.15 | -48.8% | 55.42 | 25.56 | -53.9% |
| Pro TP1 T8 | 148.32 | 69.06 | -53.4% | 21.03 | 19.05 | -9.4% |
| Pro TP1 T64 | 148.83 | 69.15 | -53.5% | 33.57 | 36.87 | +9.8% |
| Pro TP16 T1 | 178.02 | 91.13 | -48.8% | 49.86 | 19.74 | -60.4% |
| Pro TP16 T8 | 147.18 | 68.53 | -53.4% | 16.41 | 13.89 | -15.3% |
| Pro TP16 T64 | 147.56 | 69.20 | -53.1% | 22.45 | 20.01 | -10.9% |

Against fresh legacy **before** measurements, new eager remains +92.0% to +161.6% and graph +54.0% to +201.8%; against legacy **after**, +61.2% to +172.0% eager and +24.9% to +153.7% graph. These are latency deltas `(new / reference - 1) * 100`, not throughput. Legacy drift and graph regressions must not be hidden by selecting the fastest run. Earlier runs sometimes improved TP1/T64 graph latency, so no general graph speedup is claimed. A Python/native capture-boundary ablation did not materially fix the large-shape gap.

**CPU/static:** 229 adapter/cache UT cases and nine exact-source production dispatch cases passed in an isolated CPU harness. Native local collection remains blocked by the installed vLLM lacking `CircularBufferSpec`, not reported as a full suite pass. Targeted mypy using the CPU torch environment passed. Full `bash format.sh ci` passed using the configured lint virtualenv, including actionlint. The new headers were also manually clang-formatted because the hook excludes csrc.

Reproduction scripts, original tensors, positive/negative logs, exact-source archive and profiler CSV/trace data are retained in host 156's `/home/wangshaojun/pr15994-shared-validation-20261021/optimization-20261021` and the local Blue Zone evidence bundle. Legacy uses the archived `49091f0db81d41d7604cd9f84f825e5a9b58d58b` snapshot without `.git`, not a newly verified checkout HEAD.

issues.title: [v0.30.0][BugFix][Quantization] Honor W4A4 MXFP4 SwiGLU limits with unfused activation
issues.body:
Backport of #19680 for `releases/v0.30.0`.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The W4A4 MXFP4 GMM+SwiGLU+quant kernel does not accept a clamp limit, but the MoE dispatcher selected it for SiLU even when `swiglu_limit > 0`. This silently skipped the configured clipping.

For W4A4 MXFP4 with a positive limit, select the existing separate GMM1 → clipped activation → MXFP4 activation quantization → GMM2 path. Preserve the fused path for nonpositive limits and leave other quantization paths unchanged. No CANN API or serving argument is added.

This matches the clipping order in [DeepSeek-V4-Pro's official `Expert.forward`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro/blob/b5968e9190ef611bbf34a7229255be88a0e937c1/inference/model.py#L596-L606): cap gate at +limit, clamp up to [-limit, +limit], then compute SiLU(gate) * up before down projection. In particular, the gate has no lower clipping bound, and clipping is not applied to the final SwiGLU output.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Positive SwiGLU limits are now honored on the W4A4 MXFP4 routed-expert path. This uses separate operators and an intermediate tensor, so it can cost additional latency and memory versus the fused kernel. End-to-end performance has not been measured.

### How was this patch tested?

- Remote regression suite: **36 tests passed** per branch, running the exact changed module and full `test_moe_mlp.py` file in an isolated process with installed Ascend-image dependencies. On the unmodified baseline, the new positive-limit regression fails for both FP32 and BF16, demonstrating the missing fallback.
- Tests cover pre-activation clamp values and ordering before quantization, preservation of the negative gate tail, nonpositive-limit fused dispatch, and unchanged W8A8/W4A8/MXFP8 fused dispatch.
- Real Ascend NPU W4A4 operator chain: **4/4 cases passed** per branch: 1/8 tokens, two experts (including an empty expert), eager and ACL Graph capture/replay. Outputs matched the explicit GMM → official FP32 clamp/SiLU formula → BF16 → MXFP4 quantization → GMM reference exactly in these cases. The test inputs exercise both gate and up clipping thresholds.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full-model PD startup, task accuracy, and distributed/performance matrices have not been rerun with these branches. This PR does not claim to establish the cause of an observed model-accuracy drop.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

issues.title: Add GMMSwigluQuantV2 DSV4 W4A8 e2e coverage
issues.body:
## Summary
- keep GMMSwigluQuantV2 on the count-mode contract used by the W4A8 per-channel MoE path
- reject group_list_type=0 at the torch adapter boundary so the fused v2 op does not silently return mismatched results for cumsum input
- add a DSV4 W4A8 per-channel e2e operator test that loads real ModelSlim new-version w1/w3 expert weights, converts them through the same NZ/int32 + scale/bias layout, and compares fused v2 against the MoE small-op sequence

## Validation
- rebuilt vllm_ascend_C on 173.131.1.2 with SOC_VERSION=ascend910b4
- W4A8 ModelSlim per-channel direct compare, count mode, experts [0,1,2,3], counts [2,3,1,4], clamp 0.05: qmax=1, dqmax=0.00016533397138118744
- W4A8 ModelSlim per-channel direct cumsum input now fails fast with: grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2 only supports count-mode group_list
- added e2e regression: tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2_dsv4_w4a8.py
- current library result for the new e2e on 173.131.1.2: 1 passed, 1 failed; failing clamp-stress-one-token-per-expert has qmax=2 against the small-op reference, so fused v2 precision is still not fully aligned
- checked upstream/main build_aclnn.sh: grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2 is already included for ascend910b and ascend910_93
- vLLM version: v0.20.2

issues.title: [BugFix][Quantization] Pad odd W4A8-MXFP4 MoE down_proj scale groups under TP
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`AscendW4A8MXFPDynamicFusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` reshapes `w2_weight_scale`'s
last dimension into pairs of MX groups. A TP shard can leave
`intermediate_size_per_partition // group_size` odd (e.g. `moe_intermediate_size=2304`,
`group_size=32`, `tensor_parallel_size=8` gives `288 // 32 = 9`), which crashes the reshape
with a shape mismatch.

This is the same class of bug as #20398 / #20573 (DS-original W8A8 MXFP8 linear path hitting
an odd scale-group count under TP), just in the FP4 MoE routed-expert path. Pads with one
zero group before reshaping, mirroring that fix and vLLM upstream's own MXFP4 scale-alignment
pad (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/mxfp4_utils.py`).

**Caveat (updated):** unlike the W8A8 MXFP8 fix, this only pads `w2_weight_scale`, not
`w2_weight` itself. I looked for a kernel-side shape check that could make this unsafe, the
way I was burned on a since-closed sibling PR (#21398) where a kernel turned out to hardcode a
contract I'd assumed was a bug. The actual GEMM2 kernel this scale feeds into is closed-source
(`torch_npu`/CANN binary, no Python wrapper to inspect), so I can't rule that out by reading
source the way I could there.

What I *can* show: for this model specifically, this PR's precondition (odd scale-group count)
and #21397's precondition (`intermediate_size_per_partition` not a multiple of 64, i.e. SwiGLU
activation width not 128-aligned) are mathematically the same condition in disguise —
`intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 == 0` implies `(intermediate_size_per_partition / 32)` is
even, and conversely an odd scale-group count implies `intermediate_size_per_partition % 64 != 0`.
So on `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` there is no tensor-parallel size at which this PR's code path runs
without also hitting #21397 first (SwiGLU quant happens before the down_proj GEMM this scale
feeds). That means I categorically cannot exercise the padded scale in a real GEMM2 call on this
model until #21397 is also fixed — not a coincidence of which crash I hit first, a property of
`moe_intermediate_size=2304` / `group_size=32`. The fix is not model-specific, though: a
different W4A8-MXFP4 MoE model whose `moe_intermediate_size` doesn't share this 64/32
relationship could hit the odd-group crash without #21397's constraint, and would exercise this
code path for real.

So: confirmed correct for the crash it targets (unit test + real hardware), but end-to-end
correctness of the padded scale inside the actual down_proj GEMM remains unverified and, for
this specific model, unverifiable until #21397 is resolved too. Flagging for reviewers rather
than claiming full correctness.

Fixes #21396

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's W4A8-MXFP4 MoE weight loading no longer crashes when a TP shard
leaves an odd scale-group count. A release-note fragment is included (release_notes/fragments/21399.yaml).

### How was this patch tested?

- Added `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w4a8/test_w4a8_mxfp4.py::TestAscendW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod::test_process_weights_pads_odd_tp_scale_groups`,
  covering a `(8, 128, 9)` scale shard; confirmed it reproduces the exact crash
  (`RuntimeError: shape '[8, 128, 4, 2]' is invalid for input of size 9216`) against the
  unpatched code, and passes with the fix. Also added a round-trip check that
  `restore_weights_for_rl_loading` drops the padding correctly instead of crashing (caught by
  Gemini Code Assist's review — the first version of this fix only handled the forward
  direction).
- Ran the full `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w4a8/test_w4a8_mxfp4.py` suite (24 tests) — all pass.
- Verified on real A5 hardware (TP=8, native FP8 `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` checkpoint): this
  fix clears the reshape crash and weight loading completes (see caveat above for what's not
  yet verified beyond that).
- `git diff --check`, `codespell`, and `ruff` (matching the repo's pinned `v0.14.0`) pass on
  the changed files.
